ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows multiple labeled inflorescence types. The figure labeled A branches out many longer small pedicels at the top of a common flower stalk; these small pedicels radiate upward and outward from approximately the same point, forming an approximately flat-topped or dome-shaped flower cluster at the top. Reasoning: The question asks for the inflorescence type in which “individual pedicels grow out from about the same point and form a flat-topped or rounded flower cluster.” According to the structure of A in the figure and botanical terminology, this type of inflorescence is called umbel.
